# Umbaly Cloud

Umbaly Cloud is a robotics company specializing in construction site automation, with a flagship product called TieBot. TieBot is an autonomous rebar tying robot designed to increase both the speed and consistency of rebar tying operations on commercial construction projects. By automating this labor-intensive task, TieBot reduces project timelines, lowers labor costs, and improves safety by minimizing workers’ exposure to repetitive strain and hazardous site conditions.

Umbaly Cloud primarily serves commercial construction contractors operating mid- to large-scale projects across the United States. Typical customers include general contractors and specialty subcontractors responsible for concrete and structural steel work. These firms deploy TieBot to accelerate slab and foundation work, often realizing a 30-40% reduction in tying time per rebar grid compared to manual methods.

Since launching TieBot commercially in late 2022, Umbaly Cloud has deployed units on 120 active job sites nationwide, including several projects exceeding $50 million in value. The company completed a $15 million Series A funding round in Q1 2024 led by Redstone Ventures, enabling expansion of product engineering and customer success teams.

The core team includes CEO and co-founder Xanrel Mirov, who previously led robotics software at a warehouse automation startup; CTO Kelaly Shah, an expert in computer vision and autonomous systems; and Director of Field Operations Jortun Glimtun, with over a decade of experience managing construction technology deployments. Umbaly Cloud maintains a 30-person team, combining engineering, sales, and site support roles.

Key competitors include SteelBind Robotics, which offers a semi-autonomous tying tool requiring operator input, and RebarBot Solutions, notable for their drone-assisted tying but lacking full autonomy. Umbaly Cloud differentiates through fully autonomous operation and integration with existing site workflows.

Open risks include adoption resistance from traditional trades, variability in job site conditions potentially affecting robot performance, and ongoing hardware durability challenges in harsh environments. The company continues to invest in robotics robustness and customer training programs to mitigate these risks.
